How to Get Your Brand Cited by ChatGPT, Gemini & Perplexity

Let me ask you something honest: when did you last Google something important before making a decision? For a lot of people, the answer is changing. Instead of typing into Google and scrolling through ten blue links, they are opening ChatGPT and asking a question. They are using Perplexity to research vendors. They are asking Gemini which service provider to trust. And they are accepting the answer they get without clicking through to verify it themselves. This is not a future trend. It is happening right now, every single day, with your potential customers. And here is the part that should grab your attention: if your brand is not being cited in those AI responses, you are completely invisible to those buyers at the exact moment they are ready to make a decision. That is the challenge. But it is also if you move quickly one of the biggest opportunities in digital marketing today. Why Being Cited by AI Is the New First-Page Ranking Cast your mind back to the early days of SEO. The businesses that figured out Google's algorithm early did not just get more traffic they built entire companies on that advantage. The ones who ignored it spent years trying to catch up. We are at that same inflection point right now, except the platform has changed. When someone asks ChatGPT "Who are the best web design agencies in Dubai?" the AI does not hand them a list of links to browse. It gives them a name. A recommendation. A confident, authoritative answer. And most people trust it. This new discipline getting your brand into those AI answers is called GEO: Generative Engine Optimisation. It sits alongside traditional SEO, but it plays by slightly different rules. And the businesses that understand it now are quietly building an advantage that will be very hard to close later.

How AI Models Actually Decide Who to Recommend

Before you can get cited, you need to understand how these tools think. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity do not have opinions. They have data. Enormous amounts of it. When they form a recommendation, they are essentially asking themselves: what does the reliable internet say about this brand, and how consistently does it say it? They are looking at what is written about your brand on trusted, high-authority websites, how clearly your own website explains what you do and who you serve, what customers are saying in reviews on platforms like Google and Clutch, how consistently your brand name appears alongside specific topics and services, whether your website uses structured data that helps AI read it accurately, and how active and credible your presence is on platforms like LinkedIn. Put simply: AI tools recommend brands that the internet already vouches for, clearly and consistently. Your job is to make sure the right parts of the internet are saying the right things about you — in language that AI can find, read, and trust.

Seven Strategies That Actually Work

1. Get Your Digital Foundation in Order

This is where everything starts. AI models piece together a picture of your brand from dozens of sources across the web. If those sources are contradictory, thin, or simply missing, the AI fills in the gaps badly, or ignores you entirely. Before anything else, make sure your Google Business Profile is fully completed, verified, and kept up to date with your current services and contact details. Your website should speak clearly about what you do, who your clients are, and where you operate not in clever marketing language, but in plain, direct terms. Your business name, address, and phone number should be identical everywhere your brand appears online, from Google to LinkedIn to Clutch to local directories. Any inconsistency here genuinely confuses AI systems. Think of this as the soil. Everything else you plant needs it to grow.

2. Write Content That Answers Real Questions

Here is something most businesses get wrong: they create content about themselves. AI-optimised content is about your customers' questions. AI tools pull information from content that directly and clearly answers what people are actually searching for. Not broad topics, but specific, real-world questions like "How much does a website cost in Dubai?", "What is the difference between SEO and GEO?", and "How long does it take to build an e-commerce store in the UAE?" When you answer those questions better than anyone else on the internet, AI tools start citing your content when users ask similar things. This is exactly how Perplexity surfaces answers in real time and how Gemini populates its responses. The format matters too. Use clear headings. Keep paragraphs short. Put the direct answer near the top of each section. AI models, like impatient humans, prefer content that gets to the point without making them work for it.

3. Earn Mentions From Websites That AI Already Trusts

Imagine two brands. One has been mentioned fifty times on low-quality directories that nobody reads. The other has been mentioned twice once in a respected industry publication and once in a regional news feature. AI treats the second brand as far more credible. And that is exactly how it works. The quality of who talks about you matters infinitely more than the quantity. Focus your energy on earning genuine coverage from industry blogs with real audiences, news outlets covering your sector, podcast transcripts (AI reads these), guest articles you write for authoritative sites, and relevant business publications in the UAE and beyond. Every time a trusted source mentions WebCore UAE in the context of web design, digital marketing, or technology, that association gets reinforced in the data that AI tools draw from. The more it happens, the more confident those tools become in recommending you.

4. Take Reviews More Seriously Than You Ever Have

Reviews have always been important for convincing humans. Now they are important for convincing AI too. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity actively factor in review data from Google, Trustpilot, and Clutch when assessing a brand's credibility. A business with 180 detailed, positive reviews does not just look more trustworthy to a potential customer it genuinely ranks higher in the data AI uses to form recommendations. Encourage your satisfied clients to leave reviews. Make it easy for them by sending a direct link and following up after a successful project. When reviews come in, respond to them professionally and specifically. The language inside those reviews the services mentioned, the outcomes described, the location referenced all contributes to how AI understands and categorises your brand.

5. Implement Structured Data on Your Website

This is the technical one, and it is one of the most powerful things you can do for AI visibility. Schema markup is code added to your website that tells search engines and AI tools exactly what your content means, not just what it says. It is the difference between AI reading your FAQ page and understanding it as a list of questions and answers, versus reading it as a wall of text it has to interpret. For a business like WebCore UAE, the most valuable schema types include Organization schema (confirming your business name, URL, logo, contact details, and social profiles), Service schema (marking up each of your services with descriptions and areas served), FAQ schema (turning your FAQ section into structured Q&A data), Review schema (making your testimonials machine-readable), and Breadcrumb schema (helping AI understand your site structure). When your website speaks the language AI systems are built to understand, they are far more likely to pull from it, and pull from it accurately.

6. Show Up Consistently on LinkedIn and Relevant Communities

LinkedIn has become one of the most trusted B2B content sources for AI queries. Gemini and Perplexity in particular treat LinkedIn content posts, articles, company pages, and employee profiles — as credible, authoritative signals. This does not mean posting for the sake of it. It means sharing genuine insights, writing short articles about your industry, and engaging meaningfully in conversations your potential clients are already having. Over time, this builds an authoritative presence on a platform AI models treat with significant weight. Beyond LinkedIn, consider where your clients and peers gather online. Industry forums, Reddit communities, and niche groups all generate content that AI reads and learns from. When your brand name or your team's expertise appears consistently in those conversations helpfully, not promotionally it accumulates into something AI recognises as genuine authority.

7. Pursue Wikipedia and Wikidata Presence If You Qualify

Wikipedia is one of the single most heavily weighted sources in AI training data. ChatGPT was trained significantly on Wikipedia content, and all major AI tools treat it as a gold-standard reference. If your business, its leadership, or its work has reached a level of notability that meets Wikipedia's criteria, this is worth pursuing carefully and legitimately. Even if a full Wikipedia article is not yet appropriate, ensuring your brand appears accurately in relevant references, and that your business data is correct on Wikidata, contributes meaningfully to your AI visibility over time.

What Your Own Website Needs to Get Right

Your website is where all of this comes together. It is the single most important owned asset you have for AI visibility, and most business websites are not set up to take advantage of it. Say exactly what you do, for whom, and where. AI tools struggle with vague, aspirational language. "We help businesses grow" means nothing to an AI. "We build websites and run SEO campaigns for businesses in Dubai and across the UAE" means everything. Keep your blog active and genuinely useful. A blog updated two years ago signals stagnation to AI. Fresh, relevant content signals expertise and credibility. Even one high-quality, question-answering post per month makes a real difference. Make your About page a trust document. Your experience, your team, your clients, your track record all written clearly. AI is looking for signals of credibility, and your About page is a primary place it finds them. Publish detailed case studies and testimonials. Vague praise means little. Specific results, such as "We increased organic traffic by 140% for a Dubai-based e-commerce brand in six months", give AI the factual context it needs to understand what your brand actually delivers.

GEO vs SEO: What Is Actually Different?

They work together, but they are not the same thing. Traditional SEO is about earning a position in Google's ranked results so that when a human searches, they see your link and click it. Your goal is visibility in a list. GEO, Generative Engine Optimisation, is about ensuring AI systems have enough accurate, authoritative, well-structured information about your brand that they confidently recommend you directly in their answer, before a user ever sees a list of links. The overlap is significant. Strong content, authoritative backlinks, technical website quality, and consistent brand mentions all serve both. But GEO requires you to think about how an AI reads and interprets your brand across the entire web, not just whether Google can index your pages. The businesses winning at GEO right now are not the ones with the biggest budgets. They are the clearest, the most consistent, and the most present in the places AI systems have learned to trust.

Your AI Visibility Audit

Run through this checklist honestly. It will tell you exactly where your gaps are. Google Business Profile is fully completed and verified. Website homepage clearly states your services, location, and ideal clients. Service pages use plain, specific language rather than marketing fluff. An FAQ page exists and answers real customer questions. Schema markup is implemented across key pages. Business name, address, and phone are consistent across all directories. You have an active review presence on Google, Clutch, or Trustpilot. Your blog is updated regularly with question-answering content. Your LinkedIn company page is active and complete. Some coverage exists on third-party authoritative websites. Testimonials and case studies with specific results are published on the site. If you can confidently tick most of these, you are already ahead of most UAE businesses. If you are missing more than half, there is a significant opportunity sitting right in front of you.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is GEO in digital marketing? GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimisation. It is the practice of building your brand's digital presence so that AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity cite and recommend your business in their responses, rather than just ranking you in traditional search results. How do I get my brand mentioned by ChatGPT? Build a consistent, authoritative digital footprint. Earn mentions from credible websites. Publish content that directly answers your customers' questions. Collect strong, detailed reviews. And implement structured data on your website so AI systems can read and understand your brand accurately. How long does it take to see results from GEO? There is no fixed timeline, but businesses that invest consistently in quality content, authority building, and technical optimisation typically start seeing meaningful AI visibility improvements within three to six months. Is this only relevant for large businesses? Not at all. Smaller and mid-sized businesses often see faster results because they can move quickly, target specific niches clearly, and build genuine authority in focused areas something large brands with broad messaging sometimes struggle to do.

Final Thoughts

The way your customers find and choose businesses is changing at a pace that most companies are not keeping up with. AI tools are not a novelty anymore. They are becoming the first stop for purchasing decisions, vendor research, and service comparisons. The brands that get cited by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity will not just be the most famous. They will be the ones that did the work, built the right content, earned the right mentions, structured their digital presence with intention, and showed up consistently in the places AI systems have learned to trust. You do not need a massive budget. You need clarity, consistency, and the right strategy.
